2. The appellants are aggrieved by the order dated 23.02.2022 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, dismissing their petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short Cr.P.C.), challenging the summoning order dated 02.09.2021.

sentences.text: Reason: 3.

It emerges from the material on record that the brother of respondent no.2 (one Bobby)
forcibly entered the house of a woman and attempted to rape her.
Case Crime No.706/2020 was registered against him under various provisions, including 376 of the IPC.
Appellant no.1 and his father lent their support to the victim of the above-mentioned crime.
The brother of respondent no.2, along with 50 henchmen, allegedly entered the house of the appellants, attacked them and caused serious injuries.
FIR regarding this incident was separately registered on 20.09.2020.

Thereafter, respondent no.2, on 13.10.2020, filed an application under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.
and as a result of the usual mechanical order passed by the Magistrate, Crime No.767/2020 under Sections 147, 148, 149, 323, 307, 354, 504 and 506 of IPC and Section 3(1)(x) of the S.C/S.T. Act was registered against the appellants.

4. After investigation, the police did not find any proof supporting the allegations and consequently,
a cancellation report was filed.
5. Respondent no.2-complainant filed a protest petition, in which the Special Judge has summoned the appellants.
6. That summoning order was unsuccessfully challenged by the appellants before the High Court.
7. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the record.

entities.text:
R.P.
Kapur vs. State of Punjab; 1960 SCC Online SC 21
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
State of Haryana vs. Bhajanlal;

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the High Court has apparently overlooked (i) the backdrop in which case against the brother of respondent no.2 was registered; (ii) the appellants specific plea that the subject FIR is a counter blast; and (iii) the failure to substantiate the allegations against the appellants during the investigation, resulting in the filing of a closure report.
9.

In this backdrop, it was imperative upon the High Court to examine whether the Special Judge,
while issuing the summoning order, applied his mind and whether there are sustainable reasons to subject the appellants to the agony of trial.

Since such a material aspect has not been gone into by the High Court, we set aside the impugned order dated 23.02.2022 and remit the case to the High Court to accord fresh consideration to all the contentions being raised on behalf of the parties.
10. The parties are directed to appear before the High Court on 19.04.2024.
Till the matter is decided by the High Court afresh, the trial proceedings shall remain stayed.
11. The appeal is disposed of in the above terms.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. The impugned order unveils that the High Court took notice of the decisions of this Court in R.P.
Kapur vs. State of Punjab; 1960 SCC Online SC 21 as well as in the State of Haryana vs. Bhajanlal;
1992 Supp.(1) SCC 335, to delineate the scope of interference under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and has thereafter summarily dismissed the petition on the ground that the FIR/complaint prima facie established a case against the appellants.
However, the High Court has apparently overlooked (i) the backdrop in which case against the brother of respondent no.2 was registered; (ii) the appellants specific plea that the subject FIR is a counter blast; and (iii) the failure to substantiate the allegations against the appellants during the investigation, resulting in the filing of a closure report.
9.
In this backdrop, it was imperative upon the High Court to examine whether the Special Judge,
while issuing the summoning order, applied his mind and whether there are sustainable reasons to subject the appellants to the agony of trial.
